article.title: Former Russian detainee’s sister says Stephen Hubbard ‘escaped hell’
paras: Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Russian article.

The sister of former Russian detainee Stephen Hubbard says her brother's condition is better than the family expected. The 74-year-old American was released from Russia after more than four years in detention and returned to the United States last week.

"It was incredible. I don’t even know how to describe it. It’s simply unbelievable to realize that he is free and has escaped the hell he spent nearly five years in," his sister, Patricia Hubbard, said in a recent interview with VOA.
"He underwent all the examinations and tests. Now he needs to rebuild his muscles and regain his strength," she said.

Russian forces detained Stephen Hubbard in the Russian occupied-Ukrainian town of Izium in April of 2022, where he had lived and taught English since 2014. Russia convicted him of being a mercenary and sentenced him to six to 10 years in a penal colony in October of 2024. Patricia Hubbard says her brother was never a mercenary.
"That was just a pretext to take his property," she told VOA, adding that her brother had absolutely no intention of joining the Ukrainian military or taking part in the Russia-Ukraine war.

"He hated the war. He was against it. Stephen was never a military man. Yes, he served in the U.S. Air Force, but that was not during wartime," she said. "As a child, he never got into fights. He wasn’t one of those boys who was always getting into trouble. He was a good, quiet child who took part in the [Boy] Scouts and read a great deal. He always loved books."
Patricia Hubbard told VOA that she heard of her brother's possible release about two days before it happened.

"I was told that everything could change at the last minute," she said. "They [U.S. officials] did say, expect anything to happen at the last minute because that's happened before when a country will say they're going to let someone out, then they like to torture you by not letting them out [until the] last minute."
She noted that the moment she saw her brother was special.
"We just hugged. We kept telling each other, “I love you,” over and over again. We hugged for a long time," Patricia Hubbard said.

Stephen Hubbard spent the first days in the U.S. under medical evaluation. His sister says after a medical assessment, he was sent home with a new set of clothes, new medical records, a new passport, and identification.
"When someone is taken hostage, they lose everything. Everything is stripped from them," she told VOA.
Patricia, who holds a master's in psychological counseling, said she chose not to talk to her brother about his experience in the Russian jail, where she said he was tortured.
"Some of the guards who knew only a few words in English would shout, 'Die, American, die!' while beating him," she said.

"Psychologically, he is doing much better than expected," Hubbard said. "His faith has helped him enormously. Psychologically, he has been through a great deal. But he did say one thing. He said, 'I want to be around people I know and who love me.' He said there is no love in that place. No love at all. Only darkness."
While in the Russian jail, Patricia says her brother Stephen spent most of his time in complete isolation.

"And even when someone else was nearby, they didn’t speak the same language," she told VOA. "There was no television or radio. He had no sense of time. He had absolutely no idea how much the world had changed over the past five years. All of it is a shock to him. It’s as if you had fallen into a coma and then woken up.”
zh: 一名曾被俄羅斯拘留者的姊姊表示，史蒂芬·哈伯德「逃離了地獄」
編者註：本報導翻譯自美國之音（VOA）俄語原文。
前俄羅斯被拘留者史蒂芬·哈伯德的姊姊表示，她弟弟的狀況比家人預期的還要好。這位74歲的美國人被拘留超過四年後，已從俄羅斯獲釋，並於上週返回美國。
「這簡直太不可思議了。我甚至不知道該怎麼形容。想到他終於重獲自由，逃離了那座他困守近五年的地獄，這感覺實在令人難以置信，」他的妹妹帕特里夏·哈伯德在最近接受美國之音（VOA）採訪時表示。
「他已經完成了所有檢查和測試。現在他需要重建肌肉並恢復體力，」她說。
2022年4月，俄羅斯部隊在俄軍佔領的烏克蘭小鎮伊久姆（Izium）拘留了史蒂芬·哈伯德，他自2014年起便居住於此並擔任英語教師。 2024年10月，俄羅斯以「僱傭兵」罪名判處他6至10年監禁，並將其送往流放地服刑。派翠西亞·哈伯德表示，她的哥哥從來就不是僱傭兵。
「那只是為了沒收他的財產而找的藉口，」她告訴美國之音，並補充說，她的哥哥絕對沒有任何意圖加入烏克蘭軍隊或參與俄烏戰爭。
「他厭惡戰爭。他反對戰爭。史蒂芬從來就不是個軍人。是的，他曾在美國空軍服役，但那並非在戰時，」她說。 「小時候，他從不打架。他不是那種總是惹麻煩的男孩。他是個乖巧、安靜的孩子，參加過[童]子軍，而且讀了很多書。他一直都很愛書。」
派翠西亞·哈伯德向美國之音表示，她在事件發生前約兩天就聽說了弟弟可能獲釋的消息。
「有人告訴我，一切都可能在最後一刻發生變化，」她說。 「他們［美國官員］確實說過，要做好萬事皆有可能在最後一刻發生的心理準備，因為以前就發生過這種情況：某個國家會說要釋放某人，然後卻故意拖到最後一刻才放人，以此來折磨你。」
她指出，看到哥哥的那一刻非常特別。
「我們只是擁抱了一下。我們不斷對彼此說著『我愛你』，一遍又一遍。我們擁抱了很久，」派翠西亞·哈伯德說道。
史蒂芬·哈伯德抵達美國後的頭幾天都在接受醫療評估。他的姊姊表示，經過醫療評估後，他帶著一套新衣服、新的醫療紀錄、一本新護照以及身分證明文件被送回家。
「當有人被綁架時，他們會失去一切。所有東西都被剝奪了，」她對美國之音表示。
擁有心理諮商碩士學位的帕特里夏表示，她選擇不與弟弟談論他在俄羅斯監獄的經歷——她說，他在那裡曾遭受酷刑。
「有些只會說幾句英語的衛兵，一邊毆打他，一邊大喊：『去死吧，美國人，去死吧！』」她說。
「從心理層面來看，他的狀況比預期好得多，」哈伯德說。「他的信仰對他幫助極大。心理上，他經歷了許多磨難。但他確實說過一句話。他說：『我想待在熟悉的人身邊，待在愛我的人身邊。』他說那個地方沒有愛。 完全沒有愛。只有黑暗。」
帕特里夏表示，在俄羅斯監獄服刑期間，她的哥哥史蒂芬大部分時間都處於完全隔離的狀態。
「即使附近有人，他們也說著不同的語言，」她告訴美國之音。「那裡沒有電視或廣播。他完全沒有時間概念，也完全不知道過去五年來世界發生了多大的變化。 這一切對他來說都是巨大的衝擊。就好像你曾陷入昏迷，然後突然醒來一樣。」
